parsed.explanation: Combined regime criminalises transgender visibility as pornography and bans gender-reassignment propaganda; foreign attendees at LGBT events are threatened with expulsion; police detain, beat and collect data on LGBTQ people; prisons staff encourage sexual blackmail/abuse; no anti-discrimination, hate-crime, regional recourse. Absent border/care details are open questions, not safety. If outed, a visitor faces arbitrary detention, coercive prosecution/expulsion and violence, with little remedy. Death penalty is retained generally but trans-specific execution is not documented. Adult with minor adds child-involvement/prosecution uncertainty.

entry_documents.exposure: No border gender-marker rules documented. Foreign visitors at LGBT workshops were threatened with immediate expulsion under intervention-in-domestic-affairs; secondary checks could escalate into detention.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport checks, hotel IDs or cruising data collection can feed the same police/expulsion machinery; document mismatch acceptance unknown.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented September 2024 detentions include eight transgender people; police beatings, coerced charges, custody physical/psychological abuse; prison staff encourage blackmail and sexual abuse; foreign event attendees expelled.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention likely follows cruising, event attendance or document/data checks; state-run custody makes violence the operative exposure, not an off-state hazard.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National law treats trans public presence as criminal material; capital/provincial venues raided/closed; prison facilities are birth-sex/abuse-prone; no identity-matching protections.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local bars, cruising sites, prisons and subnational police enforce the national criminal frame; travellers enter the same state facilities when stopped or detained.

care_services.exposure: No documented traveller-facing care denial; psychological/trans care is scarce, trans-specific facilities are undocumented, and hostile state framing surrounds transition.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care, medication or minors could require disclosure intersecting criminalised transition advocacy; visitor procedures are not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Transgender visibility/pornography/propaganda laws, non-traditional decree, traditional-values security concept and state media frame trans people as criminal and paedophilic; police beat and collect data.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Criminal framing makes visible transition, event attendance, phone content, partner status or public presence evidence for detention/prosecution/expulsion.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented specifically; children involvement in pornography carries up to 13 years, transition advocacy is banned, so a trans minor/guardian may face prosecution or expulsion.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family document checks, school/health/travel or public presence could expose child/guardian; no child-specific protections or care rules are documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Open trans people face harassment/violence; police do not register brutality or investigate motive; they collect passports/photos at cruising; venues are raided; state demonisation supports hostility.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting violence can trigger police data collection/expulsion; calling police is not protective for a visibly trans visitor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination/hate-crime protections, no regional HR court, no official data; border/documents, 2026 propaganda application and visitor care remain unknown.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Complaints are ineffective; civil-society is only source; unknowns are open questions, not mitigation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: criminalised presentation, visitor exposure, beatings/coerced charges, illusory recourse. Our dossier has less documented routine border arrest but broader law treating trans public presence itself as pornography/propaganda, a continuous national exposure.

Similar: morality-style targeting, detentions, beatings, coerced charges, no credible capital link. The dossier names transgender people as criminal material and documents trans detentions/prison sexual abuse, so it sits at the severe end of this tier.

Higher than lethal-registry anchors: no trans-specific execution or military-deception death penalty documented. Death penalty is retained generally, but operative visitor risk is detention, prosecution/expulsion and abuse rather than capital campaign.

Below 0.25 extortion/short-jail anchors: our law criminalises trans visibility as pornography, enforcement includes trans detentions, prison staff encourage sexual abuse, and foreign attendees face expulsion; remedies are absent.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national criminalisation plus local enforcement. If a visitor is visibly transgender, attends events, is checked at cruising venues, or is processed in police/prison custody, exposure moves immediately to detention, beatings, coerced charges, expulsion or sexualised custody violence. There is no functioning protective apparatus; unknowns about border documents and care do not offset the documented targeting. Minors/guardians amplify uncertainty because children-involved penalties and transition-advocacy bans could create severe prosecution or expulsion risk.
